1  Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents 1, 2 and 5 to pay all the retirement benefits including pension, commutation value of pension etc. due to the petitioner for the 38 years of service rendered by him in terms of the proceedings dated 30.07.2015 of the designated officer,
Tirunelveli, of the second respondent department together with 18% interest per annum, within a time frame fixed by this Court.
!For Petitioner : Mr.D.Selvaraj

For Respondents : Mr.R.Anandharaj,
 Government Advocate for  R1 to R3, R5 and R6  Mr.Aayiram K.Selvakumar, 
 Government Advocate for R4  :ORDER

In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, the State of Tamil Nadu, represented by its Secretary to Government, Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department, Fort St.George,
Chennai-600 009, is suo motu impleaded as the sixth respondent in this writ petition.
2.The petitioner joined as Health Assistant in the Palayamkottai Municipality on 17.08.1976.
The post of Health Assistant was re-designated as Sanitary Officer in 1990.
Palayamkottai Municipality became a part of Tirunelveli Municipal Corporation in 1994.
In 2010, the petitioner was appointed as Food Inspector in the Tirunelveli Municipal Corporation.
3.While so, Food Safety and Standards Authority Act, 2006 came into force in 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority Act, 2006
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner was appointed as Food Safety Officer by the second respondent on 20.09.2011.
He retired in the said post on 31.08.2014 on reaching the age of superannuation.
4.The grievance of the petitioner is that his benefits are not settled.
According to him, the third respondent sent a letter dated 02.09.2014 to the second respondent stating that only respondents 1 and 2 have to settle the retirement benefits of the petitioner.
But the second respondent wrote a letter dated 09.09.2014 to the third respondent to settle the retirement benefits of the petitioner.

Hence, he has come up before this Court with this writ petition.
5.Heard the learned counsel on either side.
6.Taking into account the aforesaid facts, I am of the view that an employee who rendered 38 years of unblemished record of service could not be thrown from pillar to post for his retirement benefits.

Therefore, all the respondents including Respondent No.6, the impleaded respondent, are directed to see that his retirement benefits are settled within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
